subproblem.title: Blow-up of a rectifiable current at almost every point (printed (7))
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and let (M, θ, ξ) satisfy IsRectifiableTriple ℝ^P n M θ ξ. Then for Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. x (Hⁿ = μHE[n]) the following holds: for every linear subspace Q ⊆ ℝ^P with HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x Q and every continuous compactly supported ω : ℝ^P → Λⁿ(ℝ^P), τ(M,θ,ξ)(y ↦ r^{−n}·ω(r⁻¹(y − x))) → θ(x)·∫_Q ξ(x)(ω(z)) dHⁿ(z) as r → 0⁺. Here τ(M,θ,ξ)(η) = tauAction n M θ ξ η = ∫_M θ(y) ξ(y)(η(y)) dHⁿ(y).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (M : Set (Eucl P)) (θ : Eucl P → ℝ) (ξ : Eucl P → NVector (Eucl P) n), IsRectifiableTriple (univ : Set (Eucl P)) n M θ ξ → ∀ᵐ x ∂((μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)).restrict M), ∀ Q : Submodule ℝ (Eucl P), HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x Q → ∀ ω : Eucl P → Covector (Eucl P) n, Continuous ω → HasCompactSupport ω → Tendsto (fun r : ℝ => tauAction n M θ ξ (fun y => (r ^ n)⁻¹ • ω (r⁻¹ • (y - x)))) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 (θ x * ∫ z in (Q : Set (Eucl P)), ξ x (ω z) ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P))))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: conditions (G1)–(G2) of Step 2 and Step 3 of the parent proof, i.e. the printed display (7) of the Proof of 8.2, "η_{x,λ#}T ⇀ θ(x)[[T_x M]] as λ ↓ 0", with the documented correction that "for Lⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M" means Hⁿ-a.e. Here the blow-up is stated for the dilations η_{x,r}(y) := r⁻¹(y − x) = blowUpMap x r y, without the rotation Q_0. Its value on ω is τ(M,θ,ξ)(η_{x,r}^#ω), and (η_{x,r}^#ω)(y) = r^{−n}ω(η_{x,r}(y)).

Conventions.
- ℝ^P := Eucl P and Hⁿ := μHE[n]; B̄_s(x) is the closed ball.
- n-vectors are elements of NVector = the continuous dual of the n-covectors. ‖w‖ is the operator norm of an n-vector and ‖α‖ that of a covector, so |w(α)| ≤ ‖w‖‖α‖.
- τ(M,θ,ξ)(η) := tauAction n M θ ξ η = ∫_M θ(y) ξ(y)(η(y)) dHⁿ(y).

1. Bound on ξ. By the orients field of IsRectifiableTriple, for Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ M we have ξ(y) = ±simpleNVector τ_y with τ_y orthonormal. simpleNVector v is defined by mkContinuous with bound ∏_i ‖v_i‖, so ‖simpleNVector v‖ ≤ ∏_i ‖v_i‖. Hence ‖ξ(y)‖ ≤ 1 for Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ M. (The accepted declaration Submission.fiw_ims_tt_unit_bound, |w α| ≤ ‖α‖ for w = ±simpleNVector τ with τ orthonormal, gives the same.)

2. The weighted measure λ.
 (2a) Definition. λ(A) := ∫⁻_{M∩A} θ dHⁿ, i.e. λ := (μHE[n]⌞M).withDensity(ENNReal.ofReal ∘ θ). θ is integrable on M ∩ K for every compact K (integrableOn, U = ℝ^P), so λ(K) < ∞ for compact K. Thus λ is a locally finite Borel measure on the finite-dimensional space ℝ^P.
 (2b) Same null sets. θ is AE-strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞M. It is so on each M ∩ B̄_R(0) (by integrableOn), and M = ⋃_R (M ∩ B̄_R(0)) (Mathlib aestronglyMeasurable_iUnion_iff). Since θ > 0 on M, for measurable A we have λ(A) = 0 iff Hⁿ(M ∩ A) = 0. An arbitrary λ-null set Z is contained in the measurable λ-null set toMeasurable λ Z. Hence λ-a.e. and Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. statements coincide.
 (2c) Integrability. ξ is AE-strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞M, hence for λ ≪ Hⁿ⌞M, and ‖ξ‖ ≤ 1 λ-a.e. by step 1. So ξ is locally λ-integrable. Being locally finite on ℝ^P, λ is s-finite (indeed σ-finite), as Besicovitch.vitaliFamily requires.

3. Lebesgue–Besicovitch differentiation (Simon Ch. 1, 3.23 with 3.11(3)). Apply Mathlib VitaliFamily.ae_tendsto_average_norm_sub to the Besicovitch Vitali family Besicovitch.vitaliFamily λ, composed with Besicovitch.tendsto_filterAt (closed balls B̄_s(x), s ↓ 0, tend to the filterAt x). It gives, for λ-a.e. x,
  av(s) := λ(B̄_s(x))⁻¹ ∫_{B̄_s(x)} ‖ξ(y) − ξ(x)‖ dλ(y) → 0 as s ↓ 0.
 Note ∫_{B̄_s(x)} ‖ξ − ξ(x)‖ dλ ≤ λ(B̄_s(x))·av(s), including when λ(B̄_s(x)) = 0 (then both sides are 0). By (2b) this holds for Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. x. Fix such an x for the rest of the proof; these points form the full-measure set of the statement. Let Q be a weighted approximate tangent space of (M, θ) at x, and ω : ℝ^P → Λⁿ continuous with compact support. Choose R ≥ 1 with tsupport ω ⊆ B̄_R(0) and put ‖ω‖_∞ := sup_z ‖ω(z)‖ < ∞.

4. Change of variables. For s > 0, η_{x,s} is a translation followed by the dilation z ↦ s⁻¹z. So Hⁿ(η_{x,s}(A)) = s^{−n}Hⁿ(A) for every A ⊆ ℝ^P (Mathlib MeasureTheory.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_homothety_image or Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀, together with translation invariance). Equivalently, (η_{x,s})_*Hⁿ = sⁿHⁿ. Since η_{x,s} is a measurable embedding, every S ⊆ ℝ^P and every g : ℝ^P → ℝ satisfy
  ∫_{η_{x,s}(S)} g dHⁿ = s^{−n}∫_S g∘η_{x,s} dHⁿ   (★)
 Both sides are 0 if the integrand is not integrable. (★) is exactly the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.lpf_wtc_blowup_setIntegral_image:
  ∀ Q n y r S g, 0 < r → ∫ z in blowUpMap y r '' S, g z ∂μHE[n] = (r ^ n)⁻¹ * ∫ x in S, g (blowUpMap y r x) ∂μHE[n].

5. Growth bound.
 (5a) Choose f₀ ∈ C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ) with 0 ≤ f₀ ≤ 1 and f₀ = 1 on B̄_1(0). By the definition of HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt,
  I(s) := ∫_{η_{x,s}(M)} f₀(z)θ(x + sz) dHⁿ(z) → θ(x)∫_Q f₀ dHⁿ < ∞ as s ↓ 0.
 (5b) By (★) with g(z) := f₀(z)θ(x + sz) (so g(η_{x,s}(y)) = f₀(η_{x,s}(y))θ(y)),
  I(s) = s^{−n}∫_M f₀(η_{x,s}(y))θ(y) dHⁿ(y).
 The integrand is integrable on M. Choose R₀ with tsupport f₀ ⊆ B̄_{R₀}(0). The integrand is bounded by θ·1_{B̄_{sR₀}(x)}, and θ is integrable on M ∩ B̄_{sR₀}(x) (integrableOn with K := B̄_{sR₀}(x)). It is nonnegative, and f₀∘η_{x,s} = 1 on B̄_s(x). So I(s) ≥ s^{−n}∫_{M∩B̄_s(x)} θ dHⁿ = s^{−n}λ(B̄_s(x)); here λ(B̄_s(x)) < ∞ and the Bochner and lower integrals of θ ≥ 0 over M ∩ B̄_s(x) agree.
 (5c) Hence there are C_x < ∞ and s₀ > 0 with λ(B̄_s(x)) ≤ C_x sⁿ for all s ∈ (0, s₀).

6. Normalized Lebesgue point (condition (G2)). For s ∈ (0, s₀), by steps 3 and 5,
  ε(s) := s^{−n}∫⁻_{M∩B̄_s(x)} θ(y)‖ξ(y) − ξ(x)‖ dHⁿ(y) = s^{−n}∫⁻_{B̄_s(x)} ‖ξ − ξ(x)‖ dλ ≤ C_x av(s) → 0 as s ↓ 0.
 The lower integral is finite: the integrand is ≤ (1 + ‖ξ(x)‖) λ-a.e. and λ(B̄_s(x)) < ∞. So it equals the Bochner integral ∫_{B̄_s(x)} ‖ξ − ξ(x)‖ dλ, and real-valued estimates may be taken via toReal.

7. Splitting. Fix r > 0 and put ω_r(y) := r^{−n}ω(η_{x,r}(y)).
 (7a) ω_r is continuous, tsupport ω_r ⊆ B̄_{Rr}(x), and ‖ω_r(y)‖ ≤ r^{−n}‖ω‖_∞.
 (7b) Write θ(y)ξ(y)(ω_r(y)) = θ(y)ξ(x)(ω_r(y)) + θ(y)(ξ(y) − ξ(x))(ω_r(y)). Both summands are Hⁿ⌞M-integrable: they are AE-strongly measurable (ξ is, ω_r is continuous, evaluation is continuous), bounded in absolute value by θ(y)(‖ξ(x)‖ + 1)r^{−n}‖ω‖_∞ a.e. on M (step 1), and vanish off the compact set B̄_{Rr}(x), on which θ is integrable over M.
 (7c) Hence τ(M,θ,ξ)(ω_r) = A(r) + E(r), with
  A(r) := ∫_M θ(y)ξ(x)(ω_r(y)) dHⁿ(y),  E(r) := ∫_M θ(y)(ξ(y) − ξ(x))(ω_r(y)) dHⁿ(y).

8. Error term. By (7a),
  |E(r)| ≤ ∫_{M∩B̄_{Rr}(x)} θ(y)‖ξ(y) − ξ(x)‖ r^{−n}‖ω‖_∞ dHⁿ(y) = ‖ω‖_∞ Rⁿ ε(Rr),
 and this tends to 0 as r ↓ 0 by step 6, since Rr ↓ 0.

9. Main term.
 (9a) f(z) := ξ(x)(ω(z)) defines f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ).
 (9b) A(r) = r^{−n}∫_M θ(y)f(η_{x,r}(y)) dHⁿ(y) = ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f(z)θ(x + rz) dHⁿ(z), by (★) with g(z) := f(z)θ(x + rz); note x + r·η_{x,r}(y) = y.
 (9c) η_{x,r}(M) = blowUpMap x r '' M. By HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x Q applied to f, A(r) → θ(x)∫_Q f dHⁿ = θ(x)∫_Q ξ(x)(ω(z)) dHⁿ(z) as r ↓ 0.

10. By steps 7–9, tauAction n M θ ξ (y ↦ r^{−n}·ω(r⁻¹(y − x))) = A(r) + E(r) → θ(x)∫_Q ξ(x)(ω(z)) dHⁿ(z) as r → 0⁺. This holds for every such Q and ω, at every x of the full-measure set fixed in step 3. ∎

proof_key_steps: ‖ξ‖ ≤ 1 Hⁿ-a.e. on M (orients field and the mkContinuous bound of simpleNVector).
λ := θHⁿ⌞M is a locally finite measure with the same null sets as Hⁿ⌞M, and ξ ∈ L¹_loc(λ).
Besicovitch differentiation: the λ-averages of ‖ξ − ξ(x)‖ over B̄_s(x) tend to 0 for a.e. x.
At a weighted tangent space, testing with f₀ = 1 on B̄_1 gives λ(B̄_s(x)) ≤ C_x sⁿ; hence s^{−n}∫_{M∩B̄_s(x)} θ‖ξ − ξ(x)‖ → 0.
Split τ(M,θ,ξ)(ω_r) = A(r) + E(r) with |E(r)| ≤ ‖ω‖_∞Rⁿε(Rr) → 0.
A(r) = ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} ξ(x)(ω(z))θ(x + rz) dHⁿ by the change of variables (lpf_wtc_blowup_setIntegral_image), which tends to θ(x)∫_Q ξ(x)(ω) by the weighted tangent definition.

subproblem.title: A rectifiable current with almost everywhere integer multiplicity is integer multiplicity
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P, T ∈ D_n(U), and let (M, θ, ξ) satisfy IsRectifiableTriple U n M θ ξ with T(ω) = τ(M,θ,ξ)(ω) = tauAction n M θ ξ ω for all ω ∈ D^n(U). If θ(x) is a natural number for Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. x (Hⁿ = μHE[n]), then T is integer multiplicity.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (M : Set (Eucl P)) (θ : Eucl P → ℝ) (ξ : Eucl P → NVector (Eucl P) n), IsRectifiableTriple U n M θ ξ → (∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, T ω = tauAction n M θ ξ ω) → (∀ᵐ x ∂((μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)).restrict M), ∃ k : ℕ, θ x = k) → IsIntegerMultiplicity T
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Step 9 of the parent proof (conclusion: remove the Hⁿ-null set where θ ∉ ℕ), stated for an arbitrary domain U.

Conventions.
- Hⁿ := μHE[n] on ℝ^P := Eucl P.
- η_{x,r}(y) := r⁻¹(y − x) = blowUpMap x r y.

1. The exceptional set. M is Hⁿ-null-measurable, so by Mathlib ae_restrict_iff'₀ the hypothesis says Hⁿ(N) = 0, where N := {x ∈ M : ¬∃ k ∈ ℕ, θ(x) = k}. Put M′ := M ∖ N.
 - θ(x) ∈ ℕ for every x ∈ M′, by construction.
 - M′ is Hⁿ-null-measurable, since M is and N is null.

2. Same current. M′ ⊆ M and Hⁿ(M ∖ M′) = Hⁿ(N) = 0, so M =ᵐ M′ for Hⁿ. Hence ∫_M h dHⁿ = ∫_{M′} h dHⁿ for every h (Mathlib setIntegral_congr_set). So tauAction n M θ ξ ω = tauAction n M′ θ ξ ω, and T(ω) = tauAction n M′ θ ξ ω for every ω ∈ D^n(U).

3. Same weighted tangent spaces. Let x ∈ ℝ^P, Q a subspace and r > 0.
 - η_{x,r} is injective, so η_{x,r}(M) ∖ η_{x,r}(M′) = η_{x,r}(N).
 - Hⁿ(η_{x,r}(N)) = r^{−n}Hⁿ(N) = 0, by scaling and translation invariance of Hⁿ (Mathlib MeasureTheory.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_homothety_image).
 - Hence the sets η_{x,r}(M) and η_{x,r}(M′) are Hⁿ-a.e. equal. So for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ),
  ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f(y)θ(x + ry) dHⁿ(y) = ∫_{η_{x,r}(M′)} f(y)θ(x + ry) dHⁿ(y).
 - The finrank condition does not involve M. So HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x Q ⟺ HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M′ θ x Q, for every x and Q.
 (Alternatively apply the comparator-accepted Submission.br_weightedTangent_congr with V := ℝ^P, θ′ := θ: Hⁿ(M Δ M′) = Hⁿ(N) = 0.)

4. Rectifiable triple. IsRectifiableTriple U n M′ θ ξ holds:
 - subset: M′ ⊆ M ⊆ U;
 - null-measurable: step 1;
 - countably rectifiable: CountablyRectifiable.mono with M′ ⊆ M;
 - positivity: θ > 0 on M′ ⊆ M;
 - integrability: θ is integrable on M′ ∩ K ⊆ M ∩ K for compact K ⊆ U (IntegrableOn.mono_set);
 - measurability: ξ is AE-strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞M′ ≤ Hⁿ⌞M;
 - orients: (Hⁿ⌞M′)-a.e. x satisfies the orients property of (M, θ, ξ), because Hⁿ⌞M′ ≤ Hⁿ⌞M. For such x the frame τ, the equation ξ(x) = ±simpleNVector τ and, by step 3, the weighted tangent space span τ of (M′, θ) at x are as required.

5. Conclusion. By steps 1, 2 and 4, (M′, θ, ξ) witnesses IsIntegerMultiplicity T. ∎

Self-contained, using Mathlib scaling of μHE. The accepted Submission.br_weightedTangent_congr is an optional alternative for step 3.
proof_key_steps: N := {x ∈ M : θ(x) ∉ ℕ} is Hⁿ-null (ae_restrict_iff'₀); set M′ := M ∖ N.
τ(M′,θ,ξ) = τ(M,θ,ξ) = T, since M′ =ᵐ M.
η_{x,r}(M) and η_{x,r}(M′) differ by the null set η_{x,r}(N), so the weighted tangent spaces of (M,θ) and (M′,θ) coincide.
(M′,θ,ξ) is a rectifiable triple with θ ∈ ℕ on M′, so T is integer multiplicity.

audit.reason: Removing the null exceptional set preserves the current action and every rectifiable-triple field. Hausdorff-null preservation under blow-ups verifies tangent-space invariance explicitly, including the unchanged pointwise weight. The resulting carrier has natural-valued multiplicity everywhere, exactly as IsIntegerMultiplicity requires.

subproblem.title: A constant multiple c[[U]] of an open subset of ℝⁿ is integer multiplicity only if c ∈ ℤ
subproblem.statement: Let m ∈ ℕ, n := m+1, U ⊆ ℝⁿ open and nonempty, c ∈ ℝ, and X ∈ D_n(U) integer multiplicity with X(ω) = c∫_U ω(x)(e_1,…,e_n) dx for every ω ∈ D^n(U), where e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1 and dx is Lebesgue measure. Then c ∈ ℤ.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (m : ℕ) (U : Set (Eucl (m + 1))) (c : ℝ) (X : GeometricCurrentOn U (m + 1)), IsOpen U → U.Nonempty → IsIntegerMultiplicity X → (∀ ω : TestFormOn U (m + 1), X ω = c * ∫ x in U, (ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl (m + 1)) (m + 1)) x (fun i => EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ)) ∂volume) → ∃ k : ℤ, c = k
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the second half of Step 8 of the parent proof ("By iwl_top_dim_integrality, c[[B_1ⁿ(0)]] is i.m. … therefore c ∈ ℤ"), stated for an arbitrary nonempty open U ⊆ ℝⁿ. This is the final line of the printed Proof of 8.2: "θ ≡ θ(x) in B_1ⁿ(0); thus θ(x) ∈ ℤ".

Conventions.
- n := m + 1 and ℝⁿ := Eucl n with standard basis e = (e_1, …, e_n), e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1.
- Hⁿ := μHE[n] on ℝⁿ. It equals Lebesgue measure (Mathlib EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume).
- "i.m." means IsIntegerMultiplicity.

1. Representation. Since X is i.m., there are M″ ⊆ U, θ″ and ξ″ with:
 - IsRectifiableTriple U n M″ θ″ ξ″;
 - θ″(y) ∈ ℕ for y ∈ M″ (and θ″ > 0 there);
 - X(ω) = ∫_{M″} θ″(y)ξ″(y)(ω(y)) dy for every ω ∈ D^n(U).

2. The orientation is ±e_1∧⋯∧e_n. Let vol be the determinant of the standard basis e (Basis.det, an AlternatingMap), made a continuous alternating map (AlternatingMap.mkContinuous, or toContinuousAlternatingMap, in finite dimension). Then vol(e) = 1, and every n-covector α on ℝⁿ satisfies α = α(e)·vol (Mathlib AlternatingMap.eq_smul_basis_det, applied to α.toAlternatingMap). By the orients field there is an Hⁿ-null N₁ such that for y ∈ M″ ∖ N₁ we have ξ″(y) = ±simpleNVector τ_y for some orthonormal family τ_y of n vectors in ℝⁿ. For such y and every α,
  ξ″(y)(α) = ±α(τ_y) = ±α(e)·vol(τ_y) = σ″(y)·α(e), with σ″(y) := ±det_e(τ_y).
 det_e(τ_y)² = det(Gram matrix of τ_y) = det(I) = 1, so σ″(y) ∈ {1, −1}. Alternatively: the orthonormal family τ_y of n = dim ℝⁿ vectors is an orthonormal basis (basisOfOrthonormalOfCardEqFinrank), and Mathlib OrthonormalBasis.det_to_matrix_orthonormalBasis_real gives det_e(τ_y) = ±1. Moreover σ″(y) = ξ″(y)(vol) for y ∈ M″ ∖ N₁, so σ″ is AE-strongly measurable on M″, because ξ″ is.

3. Testing with a·vol. Let a ∈ C_c^∞(ℝⁿ) with tsupport a ⊆ U. Then ω := a·vol is in D^n(U), and ω(y)(e) = a(y).
 - By the hypothesis on X: X(ω) = c∫_U a(y) dy.
 - By steps 1 and 2: X(ω) = ∫_{M″} θ″(y)σ″(y)a(y) dy.
 Hence ∫_U g(y)a(y) dy = 0 with g := c·1_U − 1_{M″}θ″σ″, for every such a.

4. Fundamental lemma.
 - g is locally integrable on U: θ″ is integrable on M″ ∩ K for compact K ⊆ U (integrableOn), |σ″| = 1 a.e. on M″, and σ″ is AE-strongly measurable.
 - By the fundamental lemma of the calculus of variations on the open set U (Mathlib IsOpen.ae_eq_zero_of_integral_contDiff_smul_eq_zero), g = 0 Lebesgue-a.e. on U.

5. Conclusion.
 - If c = 0, then c = (0 : ℤ).
 - Assume c ≠ 0. On U ∖ M″, g = c ≠ 0, so Lⁿ(U ∖ M″) = 0.
 - U is open and nonempty, so Lⁿ(U) > 0.
 - Hence the set of y ∈ U ∩ M″ ∖ N₁ with g(y) = 0 has positive measure, in particular it is nonempty. For such y, c = θ″(y)σ″(y) with θ″(y) ∈ ℕ and σ″(y) ∈ {±1}.
 - So c = ±θ″(y) ∈ ℤ, i.e. c = k for some k ∈ ℤ. ∎

Uses only Mathlib (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume, AlternatingMap.eq_smul_basis_det, OrthonormalBasis.det_to_matrix_orthonormalBasis_real, IsOpen.ae_eq_zero_of_integral_contDiff_smul_eq_zero).
proof_key_steps: X = τ(M″,θ″,ξ″) with θ″ ∈ ℕ on M″.
For a.e. y ∈ M″, ξ″(y)(α) = σ″(y)α(e) with σ″(y) = ±det_e(τ_y) ∈ {±1}.
Testing with a·vol: ∫_U (c·1_U − 1_{M″}θ″σ″)·a = 0 for all a ∈ C_c^∞(U).
Fundamental lemma: c·1_U = 1_{M″}θ″σ″ a.e. on U.
If c ≠ 0, then Lⁿ(U ∖ M″) = 0 and some y ∈ M″ ∩ U has c = θ″(y)σ″(y) ∈ ℤ.

subproblem.title: Diagonal selection of a weakly convergent sequence with a mass bound
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U, W ⊆ ℝ^P with closure W compact, X_{k,j} ∈ D_n(U) (k, j ∈ ℕ), functions Z_k, L : D^n(U) → ℝ, and C ∈ ℝ. Assume that for every ω ∈ D^n(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W, X_{k,j}(ω) → Z_k(ω) as j → ∞ (for each k) and Z_k(ω) → L(ω) as k → ∞; and that for each k, M_W(X_{k,j}) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal C for all sufficiently large j. Then there is a strictly increasing φ with M_W(X_{k,φ(k)}) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal C for all k and X_{k,φ(k)}(ω) → L(ω) for every ω ∈ D^n(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U W : Set (Eucl P)) (X : ℕ → ℕ → GeometricCurrentOn U n) (Z : ℕ → TestFormOn U n → ℝ) (L : TestFormOn U n → ℝ) (C : ℝ), IsCompact (closure W) → (∀ (k : ℕ) (ω : TestFormOn U n), tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) n) ⊆ W → Tendsto (fun j => X k j ω) atTop (𝓝 (Z k ω))) → (∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) n) ⊆ W → Tendsto (fun k => Z k ω) atTop (𝓝 (L ω))) → (∀ k, ∀ᶠ j in atTop, (X k j).massOn W ≤ ENNReal.ofReal C) → ∃ φ : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono φ ∧ (∀ k, (X k (φ k)).massOn W ≤ ENNReal.ofReal C) ∧ ∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl P) n) ⊆ W → Tendsto (fun k => X k (φ k) ω) atTop (𝓝 (L ω))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the selection argument of Step 4 of the parent proof (the printed "(8) remains valid with T_{j′} instead of T", justified by a selection argument as in Simon Ch. 2, 6.7(2)). In the parent, X_{k,j} is the push-forward of T_j by the k-th dilation, Z_k(ω) its weak limit T(η_{λ_k}^#ω) as j → ∞, and L(ω) the blow-up limit. The diagonal sequence is the parent's Y_k := X_{k,j(k)}.

Conventions.
- ℝ^P := Eucl P, and M_W(·) := massOn W.
- |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α for a covector α.
- "ω ∈ D_W" means ω ∈ TestFormOn U n with tsupport ω ⊆ W.
- C⁺ := max(C, 0), so ENNReal.ofReal C ≤ ENNReal.ofReal C⁺ and C⁺ ≥ 0.

1. Bound (F1) (comparator-accepted declaration Submission.cmb_abs_apply_le_of_massOn_le). Let Y be a current with M_W(Y) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal C, and let ω ∈ D_W with |ω(z)| ≤ ε for all z. Then |Y(ω)| ≤ C⁺ε. (Apply the declaration with B := C⁺ ≥ 0, using M_W(Y) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal C⁺.)

2. Countable dense family. By the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.cmb_exists_countable_dense_testForms (hypothesis: closure W compact), there is a countable set E ⊆ TestFormOn U n with the following properties:
 - tsupport η ⊆ W for every η ∈ E;
 - for every ω ∈ D_W and every ε > 0 some η ∈ E has |ω(z) − η(z)| ≤ ε for all z.
 E is nonempty, since 0 ∈ D_W must be approximated. Enumerate it as E = {ω_i : i ∈ ℕ}, with repetitions allowed.

3. Lipschitz bounds for Z_k and L. Let ω, ω′ ∈ D_W with |ω(z) − ω′(z)| ≤ ε for all z.
 (3a) ω − ω′ ∈ D_W, and X_{k,j}(ω) − X_{k,j}(ω′) = X_{k,j}(ω − ω′). For all large j, M_W(X_{k,j}) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal C by hypothesis, so |X_{k,j}(ω) − X_{k,j}(ω′)| ≤ C⁺ε by step 1.
 (3b) Letting j → ∞ (first hypothesis), |Z_k(ω) − Z_k(ω′)| ≤ C⁺ε.
 (3c) Letting k → ∞ (second hypothesis), |L(ω) − L(ω′)| ≤ C⁺ε.

4. Choice of φ. Fix k. Finitely many conditions hold for all sufficiently large j:
 (4a) M_W(X_{k,j}) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal C, by the hypothesis;
 (4b) |X_{k,j}(ω_i) − Z_k(ω_i)| < 1/(k+1) for each i ≤ k, by the first hypothesis.
 So there is J_k such that (4a) and (4b) hold for all j ≥ J_k. Define φ recursively by φ(0) := J_0 and φ(k) := max(J_k, φ(k−1) + 1). Then φ is strictly increasing, and (4a), (4b) hold at j = φ(k) for every k. In particular M_W(X_{k,φ(k)}) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal C for all k.

5. Convergence.
 (5a) Fix ω ∈ D_W and ε > 0. Choose i with |ω(z) − ω_i(z)| ≤ ε for all z (step 2).
 (5b) For k ≥ i:
  |X_{k,φ(k)}(ω) − L(ω)| ≤ |X_{k,φ(k)}(ω − ω_i)| + |X_{k,φ(k)}(ω_i) − Z_k(ω_i)| + |Z_k(ω_i) − L(ω_i)| + |L(ω_i) − L(ω)|
   ≤ C⁺ε + 1/(k+1) + |Z_k(ω_i) − L(ω_i)| + C⁺ε.
  The first bound is step 1 with (4a); the second is (4b), since i ≤ k; the last is (3c).
 (5c) As k → ∞, Z_k(ω_i) → L(ω_i) by the second hypothesis. So limsup_k |X_{k,φ(k)}(ω) − L(ω)| ≤ 2C⁺ε.
 (5d) Since ε > 0 is arbitrary, X_{k,φ(k)}(ω) → L(ω).

6. φ is strictly increasing (step 4), the mass bound holds for every k (step 4), and the convergence holds for every ω ∈ D_W (step 5). ∎

proof_key_steps: (F1): |Y(ω)| ≤ max(C,0)·sup|ω| when M_W(Y) ≤ ofReal C and tsupport ω ⊆ W (cmb_abs_apply_le_of_massOn_le).
A countable sup-norm-dense family {ω_i} of test forms supported in W (cmb_exists_countable_dense_testForms).
Z_k and L inherit the Lipschitz bound |·(ω) − ·(ω′)| ≤ C⁺·sup|ω − ω′|.
Choose φ(k) ≥ max(J_k, φ(k−1)+1) so that the mass bound holds and |X_{k,φ(k)}(ω_i) − Z_k(ω_i)| < 1/(k+1) for i ≤ k.
A four-term estimate gives limsup_k |X_{k,φ(k)}(ω) − L(ω)| ≤ 2C⁺ε for every ε > 0.

Passing the uniform evaluation bound through both limits supplies the needed continuity estimate for L, despite Z and L being arbitrary functions in the contract. subproblem.title: Uniform small-ball mass bounds along a subsequence (finite upper density of the limit mass measure)
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and let T_j ∈ D_n(ℝ^P) (j ∈ ℕ; GeometricCurrentOn univ n) with sup_j M(T_j) < ∞. Then there is a strictly increasing φ : ℕ → ℕ such that for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ ℝ^P (Hⁿ = μHE[n]) there are C ∈ ℝ and r₀ > 0 with the following property: for every r ∈ (0, r₀), M_{B_r(x)}(T_{φ(j)}) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(C·rⁿ) for all sufficiently large j.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (Tj : ℕ → GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Eucl P)) n), (⨆ j, (Tj j).mass) < ∞ → ∃ φ : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono φ ∧ ∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)), ∃ C r₀ : ℝ, 0 < r₀ ∧ ∀ r ∈ Ioo (0 : ℝ) r₀, ∀ᶠ j in atTop, (Tj (φ j)).massOn (ball x r) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (C * r ^ n)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Step 1 and condition (G3) of Step 2 of the parent proof. This is the documented correction to the printed Proof of 8.2: the rescaled masses of T_{j′} stay bounded because x is chosen with Θ*ⁿ(ν, x) < ∞ for a weak limit ν of the mass measures. That is what justifies the printed "(8) remains valid with T_{j′} instead of T". Steps 1–5 below supply the details.

Conventions.
- ℝ^P := Eucl P, Hⁿ := μHE[n] on ℝ^P, and B_r(x), B̄_r(x) are the open and closed balls.
- K_R := B̄_R(0) for R ∈ ℕ.
- M_W(X) := X.massOn W and M(X) := X.mass = M_{ℝ^P}(X).
- For a finite Borel measure ν on ℝ^P, Θ*ⁿ(ν, x) := dimensionalUpperDensity ν.toOuterMeasure n univ x = limsup_{r↓0} ν(B̄_r(x))/(ω_n rⁿ), where ω_n := realUnitBallVolume n = π^{n/2}/Γ(n/2 + 1) ∈ (0, ∞).
- Λ := sup_j M(T_j) < ∞.

1. Mass measures. Fix j. Every open W with compact closure satisfies M_W(T_j) ≤ M(T_j) ≤ Λ < ∞, by monotonicity of massOn in W (GeometricCurrentOn.massOn_mono). Part (R2) of the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.iwl_restriction_theory, with U := ℝ^P, then gives a Borel measure μ_j on ℝ^P with IsMassMeasure T_j μ_j, i.e. μ_j(W) = M_W(T_j) for every open W ⊂⊂ ℝ^P (every open W with compact closure). The accepted Submission.rectifiability_mass_measure_representation would serve equally. Two consequences:
 (1a) μ_j(B_r(x)) = M_{B_r(x)}(T_j) for all x ∈ ℝ^P and r ∈ ℝ. For r ≤ 0 both sides vanish, since B_r(x) = ∅ and M_∅ = 0.
 (1b) μ_j(ℝ^P) = sup_{R∈ℕ} μ_j(B_R(0)) = sup_R M_{B_R(0)}(T_j) ≤ Λ, by continuity from below along the increasing union ⋃_R B_R(0) = ℝ^P.
 So each μ_j is a finite Borel measure of total mass ≤ Λ.

2. Weak compactness on the balls K_R (Simon Ch. 1, 4.16).

Moreover there is Y ∈ D_n(ℝ^P) such that: (b) Y(ω) = X(η) whenever η(y) = r^{−n}·ω(r⁻¹(y − x)) for all y; (c) if X is integer multiplicity, so is Y; (d) if ∂X = 0 then ∂Y = 0; (e) M_W(Y) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(r^{−n})·M_{{y : r⁻¹(y−x) ∈ W}}(X) for every W ⊆ ℝ^P.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: fact (F5) of the parent proof, specialized to the dilations used in Steps 3–4. There g_λ(y) = Q_0((y − x)/λ); here g = η := η_{x,r}, η(y) = r⁻¹(y − x), without the rotation Q_0, so no rotation-invariance of the coefficient norm is needed. Parts (a)–(e) are the facts used in parent Step 4: Y_k ∈ D_n is the push-forward of T_{j(k)}, it is integer multiplicity with ∂Y_k = 0, and M_B(Y_k) ≤ λ_k^{−n}M_{B_{2λ_k}(x)}(T_{j(k)}).

Conventions.
- ℝ^P := Eucl P, n := m + 1, Hⁿ := μHE[n].
- For a covector α and a continuous linear map L, α∘L := α.compContinuousLinearMap L.
- |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α, and M_W(X) := X.massOn W.
- η(y) := r⁻¹(y − x), r > 0; its inverse is η⁻¹(z) = x + rz.

1. Pull-back formula. Let L := r⁻¹·id (a continuous linear map ℝ^P → ℝ^P) and b := −r⁻¹x, so η(y) = b + L y. For an n-covector α, (α∘L)(v_1,…,v_n) = α(r⁻¹v_1,…,r⁻¹v_n) = r^{−n}α(v_1,…,v_n) by multilinearity (MultilinearMap.map_smul_univ). Hence the SimonGMT affine pull-back is
 affinePullbackForm L b ω (y) = (ω(b + Ly))∘L = r^{−n}·ω(η(y)) =: (η^#ω)(y).

2. Test forms; part (a). η is an affine homeomorphism of ℝ^P, hence a proper map: η⁻¹(K) = x + rK is compact for compact K.
 - SimonGMT affinePullbackForm_isTestForm (AffineCurrentPushforward.lean) shows that η^#ω is smooth with compact support.
 - SimonGMT tsupport_affinePullbackForm_subset gives tsupport η^#ω ⊆ η⁻¹(tsupport ω).
 - So η^#ω ∈ D^n(ℝ^P) is the test form affinePullbackTestOn L b hproper univ n ω. Note η⁻¹(ℝ^P) = ℝ^P, definitionally (Set.preimage_univ is rfl).
 This gives (a): for every ω there is a test form whose value at every y is r^{−n}·ω(r⁻¹(y − x)).

3. Definition of Y; part (b).
 - Let Y := GeometricCurrentOn.affinePushforward L b hproper X (SimonGMT AffineCurrentPushforward.lean), regarding X as a current on η⁻¹(ℝ^P) = ℝ^P.
 - Y is a genuine current, i.e. sequentially continuous, because the pull-back is sequentially continuous in the test-form topology (TestFormOnConverges.affinePullback).
 - By affinePushforward_apply, Y(ω) = X(η^#ω).
 - If a test form η′ satisfies η′(y) = r^{−n}·ω(r⁻¹(y − x)) for all y, then η′ = η^#ω (Subtype.ext and funext), so Y(ω) = X(η′). This is (b).

4. Part (d). By SimonGMT GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_affinePushforward, which rests on exteriorDerivative_affinePullbackForm d(η^#ω) = η^#(dω), we have ∂Y = affinePushforward(∂X). If ∂X = 0, then ∂Y(ω) = ∂X(η^#ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ D^{n−1}(ℝ^P), i.e. ∂Y = 0.

5. Part (e), the mass bound.
 (5a) Let W ⊆ ℝ^P, and let ω ∈ D^n(ℝ^P) be admissible for M_W(Y): tsupport ω ⊆ W and |ω(z)| ≤ 1 for all z.
 (5b) covectorEuclideanNorm is absolutely homogeneous, |cα| = |c||α|. Its definition is the square root of the sum of squares of the coordinates α(e_I), each of which scales by c.
 (5c) Hence η̂ := rⁿ·η^#ω is a test form with η̂(y) = ω(η(y)). So |η̂(y)| ≤ 1 for all y, and tsupport η̂ ⊆ η⁻¹(tsupport ω) ⊆ η⁻¹(W) = {y : r⁻¹(y − x) ∈ W}. Thus η̂ is admissible for M_{η⁻¹(W)}(X), and ENNReal.ofReal(X(η̂)) ≤ M_{η⁻¹(W)}(X) (GeometricCurrentOn.le_massOn).

 (5e) Taking the supremum over admissible ω gives M_W(Y) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(r^{−n})·M_{η⁻¹(W)}(X). This is (e).

6. Change of variables. η is a translation followed by the dilation z ↦ r⁻¹z. Hence Hⁿ(η(A)) = r^{−n}Hⁿ(A) for every A ⊆ ℝ^P, using Mathlib MeasureTheory.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_homothety_image or Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀ and translation invariance of Hⁿ. Equivalently, η_*Hⁿ = rⁿHⁿ. Since η is a measurable embedding, every S ⊆ ℝ^P and every g : ℝ^P → ℝ satisfy
  ∫_{η(S)} g dHⁿ = r^{−n}∫_S g∘η dHⁿ   (★)
 Both sides are 0 if the integrand is not integrable. (★) is the comparator-accepted Submission.lpf_wtc_blowup_setIntegral_image, since η = blowUpMap x r. Moreover:
 - η and η⁻¹ map Hⁿ-null sets to Hⁿ-null sets;
 - for every A, Hⁿ⌞η(A) = r^{−n}·η_*(Hⁿ⌞A) as measures (evaluate on Borel sets B: Hⁿ(η(A) ∩ B) = Hⁿ(η(A ∩ η⁻¹(B))) = r^{−n}Hⁿ(A ∩ η⁻¹(B))).

 (ii) (M′, θ′, ξ′) is a rectifiable triple in ℝ^P, and θ′(z) ∈ ℕ for z ∈ M′:
  - M′ ⊆ ℝ^P trivially.
  - Null-measurability. M is a.e.-equal to a Borel set B. η(B) is Borel (η is a homeomorphism), and η(M) Δ η(B) = η(M Δ B) is Hⁿ-null by step 6. So M′ is Hⁿ-null-measurable.

  - Positivity and integrality. For z ∈ M′ we have η⁻¹(z) ∈ M, so θ′(z) = θ(η⁻¹(z)) > 0 and θ′(z) ∈ ℕ.
  - Local integrability. Let K be compact. Then η⁻¹(K) = x + rK is compact.
   * By step 6, Hⁿ⌞(M′ ∩ K) = Hⁿ⌞η(M ∩ η⁻¹(K)) = r^{−n}·η_*(Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ η⁻¹(K))).
   * θ′∘η = θ, and θ is integrable for Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ η⁻¹(K)).
   * By Mathlib MeasurableEmbedding.integrable_map_iff (η is a measurable embedding), θ′ is integrable for η_*(Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ η⁻¹(K))), hence for its multiple Hⁿ⌞(M′ ∩ K).
   So θ′ is integrable on M′ ∩ K.
  - Measurability of ξ′. By step 6, Hⁿ⌞M′ = r^{−n}·η_*(Hⁿ⌞M). ξ is AE-strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞M, so ξ′ = ξ∘η⁻¹ is AE-strongly measurable for η_*(Hⁿ⌞M) (η a measurable embedding), hence for Hⁿ⌞M′.
  - Orientation. Let y ∈ M be a point where the orients property of (M, θ, ξ) holds: τ is orthonormal, Q := span τ, HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ y Q, and ξ(y) = ±simpleNVector τ. Let z := η(y) ∈ M′. For s > 0:
   * blowUpMap z s '' M′ = {s⁻¹(η(w) − η(y)) : w ∈ M} = {(rs)⁻¹(w − y) : w ∈ M} = blowUpMap y (rs) '' M;
   * θ′(z + su) = θ(x + r(z + su)) = θ(y + (rs)u).
   Hence for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ), ∫_{blowUpMap z s '' M′} f(u)θ′(z + su) dHⁿ(u) = ∫_{blowUpMap y (rs) '' M} f(u)θ(y + (rs)u) dHⁿ(u). So HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M′ θ′ z Q holds, and ξ′(z) = ξ(y) = ±simpleNVector τ. The points y ∈ M where the orients property fails form an Hⁿ-null set, and its image under η is Hⁿ-null (step 6). So the orients property of (M′, θ′, ξ′) holds Hⁿ⌞M′-a.e.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Steps 5–8 of the parent proof, which are the printed displays (8)–(10) of the Proof of 8.2 (pp. 178–179) with the documented corrections. The final BV step is the top-dimensional case (Remark 3.12): hypothesis (TOP), followed by the sibling ind_const_multiple_integer. Here Y_k plays the role of η_{x,λ_k#}T_{j(k)}, and c[[Q]] that of σθ(x)[[L_0]].

Two presentational changes from the parent proof, neither changing the argument:
- No rotation Q_0. We work with the plane Q = span τ itself, the distance d to Q and the coordinates p with respect to τ.
- The localized currents live on the bounded cylinder W′ = {|p| < 1, d < 3/4} rather than on the infinite cylinder Ω = B_1ⁿ × ℝ^{P−n}. Their supports lie in {d ≤ γ} with γ < 3/4, so they are the restrictions to W′ of the printed Ω-currents.

Hypotheses.
- (ST) SlicingTheorem and (LPF) LipschitzPushforwardIntegerMultiplicity.
- (RWL), (SPF), (TOP): the frozen Lean types of iwl_restriction_weak_limit, iwl_smooth_pushforward and iwl_top_dim_integrality, exactly as they appear as antecedents of this theorem.
- τ : Fin n → ℝ^P orthonormal, n := m + 1, and c ∈ ℝ.
- Y_k ∈ D_n(ℝ^P) integer multiplicity with ∂Y_k = 0 and C_0 := sup_k M_B(Y_k) < ∞, where B := B_2(0) ⊆ ℝ^P.
- Y_k(ω) → c∫_Q ω(z)(τ) dHⁿ(z) for every ω ∈ D^n(ℝ^P) with tsupport ω ⊆ B, where Q := span τ and Hⁿ := μHE[n].
Goal: c ∈ ℤ.

Conventions.
- V := B_1(0) ⊆ ℝⁿ = Eucl n, and e := (e_1, …, e_n), e_i := EuclideanSpace.single i 1.
- M_W(·) := massOn W, and "i.m." means IsIntegerMultiplicity.
- (R1), (R2) denote the uniqueness and mass-measure/restriction parts of the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.iwl_restriction_theory.

0. Geometry.
 (0a) The coordinate map. p : ℝ^P → ℝⁿ, p(y) := (⟪τ_1,y⟫, …, ⟪τ_n,y⟫), packaged as a continuous linear map, e.g. (EuclideanSpace.equiv _ ℝ).symm ∘L ContinuousLinearMap.pi (fun i => innerSL ℝ (τ i)). It is C^∞ with fderiv ℝ p y = p. By Bessel's inequality (Mathlib Orthonormal.sum_inner_products_le) ‖p(y)‖ ≤ ‖y‖, so ‖p‖ ≤ 1 (opNorm_le_bound). Also p(τ_i) = e_i.
 (0b) The distance to Q. π(y) := Σ_i ⟪τ_i,y⟫τ_i ∈ Q and d(y) := ‖y − π(y)‖.
  - y − π(y) ⊥ Q, so ‖y‖² = ‖π(y)‖² + d(y)², and ‖π(y)‖ = ‖p(y)‖.
  - d is 1-Lipschitz: d(y) − d(y′) ≤ ‖(y − y′) − π(y − y′)‖ ≤ ‖y − y′‖. It is continuous, and it vanishes on Q because π(z) = z for z ∈ Q = span τ. Q is a finite-dimensional subspace, hence closed and measurable.
  - Hence ‖fderiv ℝ d y‖ ≤ 1 for every y (Mathlib norm_fderiv_le_of_lipschitz; fderiv = 0 where d is not differentiable).
 (0c) The parametrization of Q. ι : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P, ι(a) := Σ_i a_i τ_i, is a linear isometry with range Q, and p∘ι = id. By Mathlib Isometry.map_euclideanHausdorffMeasure and EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume, ∫_Q h dHⁿ = ∫_{ℝⁿ} h(ι(a)) da for every h : ℝ^P → ℝ, with Lebesgue measure da. In particular Hⁿ(Q ∩ K) < ∞ for bounded K, so Hⁿ⌞Q is locally finite.
 (0d) The cylinder. W′ := {y : ‖p(y)‖ < 1, d(y) < 3/4}.
  - W′ is open and bounded, since ‖y‖² < 1 + 9/16.
  - closure W′ ⊆ {‖p(y)‖ ≤ 1, d(y) ≤ 3/4} ⊆ B̄_{5/4}(0) ⊆ B, so W′ ⊂⊂ B (CompactlyContainedOpen W′ B), and p(W′) ⊆ V.
  - For γ < 3/4 and compact K ⊆ V, the set K′ := p⁻¹(K) ∩ {d ≤ γ} is closed and bounded (‖y‖² ≤ 1 + γ²), hence compact, and K′ ⊆ W′.

1. The limit currents.
 (1a) X(ω) := c∫_Q ω(z)(τ) dHⁿ(z) defines a current X ∈ D_n(B).
  - Hⁿ⌞Q is finite on compact sets (IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts), by (0c). So z ↦ ω(z)(τ), continuous with compact support, is Hⁿ⌞Q-integrable, and X is linear.
  - If ω_i → 0 in D^n(B), the supports lie in one compact K ⊆ B. The k = 0 clause of TestFormOnConverges together with norm_iteratedFDeriv_zero gives sup_z‖ω_i(z)‖ → 0. Hence |X(ω_i)| ≤ |c|·Hⁿ(Q ∩ K)·sup_z‖ω_i(z)‖ → 0, using |α(τ)| ≤ ‖α‖∏_j‖τ_j‖ = ‖α‖.
 (1b) Let μ_Q := Hⁿ⌞Q and let v(z) := c·simpleNVector τ (constant). For ω ∈ D^n(B), z ↦ v(z)(ω(z)) = c·ω(z)(τ) is continuous with compact support, hence μ_Q-integrable by (0c), and its integral is X(ω). So (μ_Q, v) is a measure representation of X (IsMeasureRepresentation X μ_Q v).
 (1c) Likewise S′(ω) := c∫_V ω(a)(e) da defines a current S′ ∈ D_n(V), by the same argument with Lebesgue measure on ℝⁿ.

2. Restriction of the domain to B. Let X_k := Y_k.restrictDomain (B ⊆ ℝ^P) ∈ D_n(B), so X_k(ω) = Y_k(ω).
 (2a) X_k ⇀ X in B, by the convergence hypothesis (tsupport ω ⊆ B).
 (2b) M_W(X_k) ≤ M_W(Y_k) ≤ C_0 for W ⊆ B: an admissible form for X_k gives an admissible form for Y_k with the same value.
 (2c) ∂X_k = 0, since ∂X_k(ω) = Y_k(dω) = ∂Y_k(ω) = 0.
 (2d) X_k is i.m. Write Y_k = τ(M_k, θ_k, ξ_k) with a rectifiable triple in ℝ^P and θ_k ∈ ℕ on M_k.
  - For ω ∈ D^n(B), ω = 0 off B, so X_k(ω) = tauAction(M_k ∩ B, θ_k, ξ_k)(ω). This uses Mathlib setIntegral_eq_of_subset_of_ae_sdiff_eq_zero, which needs only that M_k is null-measurable, together with the vanishing of the integrand on M_k ∖ B.
  - (M_k ∩ B, θ_k, ξ_k) is a rectifiable triple in B with integer θ_k: subset, null-measurability, countable rectifiability (mono), positivity, integrability on compact K ⊆ B (⊆ M_k ∩ K) and AE-strong measurability are inherited.
  - The orients property at a.e. y ∈ M_k ∩ B is inherited as well. B is open, y ∈ B, and (M_k ∩ B) Δ M_k does not meet B. So by the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.br_weightedTangent_congr (V := B, θ′ := θ_k), every weighted approximate tangent space of (M_k, θ_k) at y is one of (M_k ∩ B, θ_k).
  - Equivalently, (2d) is an instance of the comparator-accepted Submission.br_restrictDomain_isIntegerMultiplicity: restrictDomain to an open set preserves integer multiplicity.

3. Slicing (parent Step 5). For each k apply (ST) with U := B, T := X_k, f := d and L := 1. The hypotheses hold: for W ⊂⊂ B, M_W(X_k) ≤ C_0 < ∞ and M_W(∂X_k) = 0; and d is 1-Lipschitz. This gives slices S^k_t ∈ D_m(B), t ∈ ℝ, with the following properties.
 (3a) Slices are boundaries. IsSlice X_k d t S^k_t: there are restrictions A^k_t of X_k and Bc^k_t of ∂X_k = 0 to {y ∈ B : d(y) < t} with S^k_t = ∂A^k_t − Bc^k_t. That set is measurable: this is the first component of the IsRestriction for Bc^k_t, and also follows since the set is open. The zero current has the measure representation (0, 0), through which 0 is a restriction of the zero current to every measurable set. By (R1), Bc^k_t = 0, so S^k_t = ∂A^k_t.
 (3b) Mass bound. By (R2) there are a restriction R^k of X_k to the open set {y ∈ B : 1/4 < d(y) < 1/2} and a measure μ_k with IsMassMeasure X_k μ_k; note M_W(X_k) < ∞ for W ⊂⊂ B. Apply the slicing mass bound with W := W′ (open, ⊆ B), L_W := 1 (allowed by (0b)) and (a, b) := (1/4, 1/2). It gives a measurable g_k : ℝ → [0, ∞] with M_{W′}(S^k_t) ≤ g_k(t) for t ∈ (1/4, 1/2) and
  ∫⁻_{(1/4,1/2)} g_k ≤ M_{W′}(R^k) = μ_k(W′ ∩ {1/4 < d < 1/2}) ≤ μ_k(W′) = M_{W′}(X_k) ≤ C_0,
 by the mass identity of (R2) and IsMassMeasure, since W′ ⊂⊂ B. The slicing clause needs the derivative bound in the form ∀ᵐ y ∂volume, y ∈ W′ → ‖fderiv ℝ d y‖₊ ≤ 1. It holds for every y by norm_fderiv_le_of_lipschitz with constant 1, coerced to ℝ≥0.
 (The slices are also i.m. for a.e. t, but this is not needed below.)

4. Restriction limits (parent Step 5). Apply (RWL) with U := B, the sequence (X_k)_k, the limit X, W := W′ and φ := d. Its hypotheses hold: X_k ⇀ X by (2a), W′ is open and ⊆ B, sup_k M_{W′}(X_k) ≤ C_0 < ∞, and d is continuous. It gives a strictly increasing ψ and a countable E ⊆ ℝ with the following property: for every s ∉ E and all restrictions R_j of X_{ψ(j)} and R of X to {y ∈ B : d(y) < s}, R_j(ω) → R(ω) for every ω ∈ D^n(B) with tsupport ω ⊆ W′.

5. Choice of γ.
 (5a) By Fatou (Mathlib lintegral_liminf_le), ∫⁻_{(1/4,1/2)} liminf_k g_{ψ(k)} ≤ liminf_k ∫⁻_{(1/4,1/2)} g_{ψ(k)} ≤ C_0 < ∞. Hence liminf_k g_{ψ(k)}(t) < ∞ for a.e. t ∈ (1/4, 1/2).
 (5b) Existence of γ.
  - t ↦ liminf_k g_{ψ(k)}(t) is measurable (Measurable.liminf), and its lower integral over (1/4,1/2) is finite. So it is < ∞ for (volume⌞(1/4,1/2))-a.e. t (ae_lt_top).
  - E is countable, hence Lebesgue-null.
  - volume⌞(1/4,1/2) is not the zero measure, so a property holding for a.e. t under it holds for some t.
  Hence there is γ ∈ (1/4, 1/2) ∖ E with G₀ := liminf_k g_{ψ(k)}(γ) < ∞.
 (5c) By Filter.frequently_lt_of_liminf_lt, infinitely many k satisfy g_{ψ(k)}(γ) < G₀ + 1 =: G. So there is a strictly increasing σ with g_{ψ(σ(k))}(γ) ≤ G for all k (Mathlib Filter.extraction_of_frequently_atTop).
 (5d) Put κ := ψ∘σ, A_γ := {y ∈ B : d(y) < γ} (open) and R_k := A^{κ(k)}_γ from (3a). R_k is a restriction of X_{κ(k)} to A_γ, with ∂R_k = S^{κ(k)}_γ and M_{W′}(∂R_k) ≤ g_{κ(k)}(γ) ≤ G.

6. Properties of R_k (parent Steps 5 and 6(a)–(d)).
 (6a) X is a restriction of itself to A_γ. A_γ is measurable (open). With the representation (1b), ∫_{A_γ} v(ω) dμ_Q = ∫ v(ω) dμ_Q = X(ω) for ω ∈ D^n(B). Indeed μ_Q-a.e. z lies in Q (Q is closed; ae_restrict_mem), and every z ∈ Q ∖ A_γ lies outside B (d(z) = 0 < γ), where ω(z) = 0.
 (6b) Convergence. Apply step 4 with s := γ ∉ E to the restrictions R′_j := A^{ψ(j)}_γ of X_{ψ(j)} (from (3a)) and R := X (by (6a)). It gives R′_j(ω) → X(ω) for every ω ∈ D^n(B) with tsupport ω ⊆ W′. Along the subsequence σ, R_k(ω) = R′_{σ(k)}(ω) → X(ω).
 (6c) Mass. By the mass identity of (R2) for X_{κ(k)}, M_{W′}(R_k) = μ_{κ(k)}(W′ ∩ A_γ) ≤ μ_{κ(k)}(W′) = M_{W′}(X_{κ(k)}) ≤ C_0.
 (6d) Formula. Write X_{κ(k)} = τ(M′_k, θ′_k, ξ′_k) on D^n(B), with M′_k ⊆ B (step 2).
  - (Hⁿ⌞M′_k, θ′_kξ′_k) is a measure representation of X_{κ(k)}: for ω ∈ D^n(B), x ↦ θ′_k(x)ξ′_k(x)(ω(x)) is Hⁿ⌞M′_k-integrable (comparator-accepted Submission.ltg_tau_integrable) with integral X_{κ(k)}(ω).
  - R_k is given by some representation (μ₁, v₁) of X_{κ(k)}. The comparator-accepted declaration Submission.slicing_representation_unique says that two representations agreeing on all ω ∈ D^n(B) have equal integrals over every measurable set, for all such ω. With W := B and A := A_γ it gives
   R_k(ω) = ∫_{A_γ} θ′_kξ′_k(ω) d(Hⁿ⌞M′_k) = tauAction(M′_k ∩ A_γ, θ′_k, ξ′_k)(ω) for all ω ∈ D^n(B).
 (6e) Vanishing. If ω ∈ D^n(B) vanishes on A_γ, then R_k(ω) = 0 by (6d). In particular R_k(ω) = 0 whenever tsupport ω ⊆ {d > γ}.

7. Localization to W′ (parent Step 6, with W′ in place of Ω). Let Z_k := R_k.restrictDomain (W′ ⊆ B) ∈ D_n(W′).
 (7a) Z_k is i.m.
  - By (6d), Z_k = τ(M′_k ∩ A_γ ∩ W′, θ′_k, ξ′_k) on D^n(W′), since forms in D^n(W′) vanish off W′.
  - The triple is rectifiable in W′ with integer multiplicity: subset, null-measurability, countable rectifiability, positivity, integrability on compact K ⊆ W′ (a compact subset of B) and measurability are inherited.
  - Orients property at a.e. y ∈ M′_k ∩ A_γ ∩ W′: the open set A_γ ∩ W′ contains y and does not meet (M′_k ∩ A_γ ∩ W′) Δ M′_k. So Submission.br_weightedTangent_congr transfers the weighted tangent spaces of (M′_k, θ′_k) at y.
  - Equivalently: the same argument with the open set A_γ shows that R_k = τ(M′_k ∩ A_γ, θ′_k, ξ′_k) is i.m. on B. Then Z_k = R_k.restrictDomain is i.m. by Submission.br_restrictDomain_isIntegerMultiplicity.
 (7b) M_{W″}(Z_k) ≤ M_{W′}(R_k) ≤ C_0 for every W″: an admissible form for Z_k on W″ is admissible for R_k on W′; then use (6c).
 (7c) ∂Z_k = (∂R_k)|_{W′} = S^{κ(k)}_γ|_{W′}, so M_{W″}(∂Z_k) ≤ M_{W′}(S^{κ(k)}_γ) ≤ G for every W″ (5d).
 (7d) Z_k(ω) = R_k(ω) → X(ω) for every ω ∈ D^n(W′), by (6b).
 (7e) spt Z_k ⊆ W′ ∩ {d ≤ γ}. Every y ∈ W′ with d(y) > γ has a ball around it whose closure lies in the open set W′ ∩ {d > γ}. Z_k vanishes on all forms supported in that ball, by (6e). So y lies in the zero region of Z_k.

8. Projection (parent Step 7). For each k apply (SPF), with (LPF), to U := W′, V := B_1(0) ⊆ ℝⁿ, X := Z_k (i.m. by (7a)) and f := p. Its hypotheses hold:
 - p is C^∞ (linear) and p(W′) ⊆ V (0d).
 - Properness. Let K ⊆ V be compact and K′ := p⁻¹(K) ∩ {d ≤ γ}, compact and ⊆ W′ by (0d). Since spt Z_k = W′ ∖ zeroRegion(Z_k) ⊆ {d ≤ γ} (7e) and K′ ⊆ W′, we get p⁻¹(K) ∩ spt Z_k = K′ ∩ (zeroRegion Z_k)ᶜ. This is a closed subset (GeometricCurrentOn.isOpen_zeroRegion) of the compact set K′, hence compact.
 (SPF) gives i.m. currents S′_k ∈ D_n(V) such that:
 (8a) S′_k(ω) = Z_k(η) whenever η ∈ D^n(W′) agrees with p^#ω, (p^#ω)(y) = ω(p(y))∘p, on an open N ⊇ spt Z_k;
 (8b) for every W″ ⊆ ℝⁿ, with c := 1 ≥ ‖fderiv p‖: M_{W″}(S′_k) ≤ M_{p⁻¹(W″)∩W′}(Z_k) ≤ C_0 and M_{W″}(∂S′_k) ≤ M_{p⁻¹(W″)∩W′}(∂Z_k) ≤ G.
 Hence sup_k (M_{W″}(S′_k) + M_{W″}(∂S′_k)) ≤ C_0 + G < ∞ for every W″.

9. The limit of S′_k (parent Step 7). Fix ω ∈ D^n(V), let K := tsupport ω (a compact subset of V) and let K′ be as in (0d).
 (9a) Cutoff (smooth Urysohn lemma).
  - Choose δ > 0 with cthickening (2δ) K′ ⊆ W′ (Mathlib IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open).
  - Apply Mathlib exists_contDiff_zero_iff_one_iff_of_isClosed to the disjoint closed sets s := (thickening (2δ) K′)ᶜ and t := cthickening δ K′. It gives ζ ∈ C^∞(ℝ^P) with values in [0, 1], ζ = 1 exactly on t and ζ = 0 exactly on s.
  - Put N₀ := thickening δ K′, an open set containing K′ with ζ = 1 on N₀.
  - tsupport ζ ⊆ cthickening (2δ) K′, which is compact and contained in W′.
  - Put η := ζ·p^#ω. It is smooth with tsupport η ⊆ tsupport ζ, so η ∈ D^n(W′).
